# ERRORS.md — error-surface table

Mechanically derived from every rejection site in `c_src/src/hashmap.c`,
`c_src/src/tree.c` and `c_src/src/main.c`: every `return -1`, `return NULL`,
`return 0`-on-guard, every `if (!ptr)` guard, every `fprintf(stderr, ...)`
diagnostic, every explicit range/limit check (`MAX_CHILDREN`, `MAX_DATA_LENGTH`,
`probe < capacity`, `length < 1000`, `length > max_length`) and every `assert()`
in the driver.

Implemented in `tests/phase_c_errors.rs` (rows E1–E47, including E46, the
`assert()` block of `main.c`, and the B1–B6 boundary rows).
`[x]` = differential test written and passing against both `.so`s.

The allocation-failure branches (E1, E2, E5, E21, E25) are reached with an
`LD_PRELOAD` shim (`cbuild/failalloc.c`, generated by the test) that makes the
n-th `malloc`/`calloc` after `failalloc_arm(n)` return NULL; each case runs in a
child process for the C `.so` and for the Rust `.so` and both children's
`stdout`/`stderr`/exit status are compared.

## Boundary/robustness cases also covered (generic ABI boundaries)

| # | case | note | [x] |
|---|------|------|-----|
| B1 | NULL for every pointer parameter of all 20 library entry points | `hashmap_{put,get,remove,contains,size,clear,destroy}`, `tree_{delete,add_node,remove_node,get_node,contains,size,print,get_depth,get_height,count_descendants,find_path}` + `path == NULL` + `data == NULL` | [x] |
| B2 | `tree_id_t` extremes | `0`, `1`, `u64::MAX`, `u64::MAX-1`, `1<<63`, ids that collide in the same bucket | [x] |
| B3 | `int` extremes across the FFI boundary | `max_length` = `i32::MIN`, `-1`, `0`, `1`, `i32::MAX` | [x] |
| B4 | oversized `data` | 255, 256, 257, 300, 1024-byte C strings → truncation to 255 chars + NUL | [x] |
| B5 | zero-length `data` | `""` and `NULL` (only `data[0]` initialised — the rest of `data` stays uninitialised in **both** implementations, so only the NUL-terminated prefix is compared) | [x] |
| B6 | non-ASCII / high-bit `data` bytes | bytes `0x80..0xFF`, invalid UTF-8 — must round-trip verbatim through `printf("%s")` | [x] |
| B7 | out-of-range enum values | the C API declares **no** `enum` and no flag/mode parameter; the only non-pointer, non-integer-range inputs are `tree_id_t` (full `u64` range, all valid) and `int max_length` (full `int` range, covered by B3). Nothing to reject. | n/a |

## Documented C undefined behaviour — deliberately not exercised

These are *not* rejections; the C code has no guard and would crash or read
out of bounds. A differential test would only compare two crashes, so they are
listed for completeness instead:

* `hashmap_put/get/remove` with a hand-built `hashmap_t` whose `capacity == 0`
  → `hash % 0` (SIGFPE in C, panic in Rust).
* `hashmap_*` / `tree_*` with a non-NULL but invalid (dangling) pointer.
* `tree_delete` with `tree->node_map == NULL`, or `tree_*` on a `tree_t` whose
  `node_map` is invalid.
* A hand-built `tree_node_t` with `child_count > MAX_CHILDREN` → reads past
  `child_ids` in C.
* A hand-built `tree_node_t` with a **negative** `child_count`: C's
  `child_count >= MAX_CHILDREN` is false, so `child_ids[child_count++]` writes
  *before* the array (heap corruption). The translation rejects it instead
  (`child_count as usize >= MAX_CHILDREN`); every value reachable through the
  API (0..=32) behaves identically.
* Use-after-`tree_delete` / use-after-`hashmap_destroy`.
* A parent chain that *cycles* without reaching `root_id`: `tree_get_depth`
  would spin forever in both implementations. Reachable only by mutating
  `parent_id` by hand (`tree_add_node` never creates one). The *non-cyclic*
  variants of a broken chain are covered by rows E32/E33/E40, and the
  `length < 1000` cap of `tree_find_path` by row E47.
